name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Lasher's large fundraising and outside spending advantage
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: This Manhattan seat carries a D+33 partisan lean, and Micah Lasher has raised over $3.3 million with more than $10 million in outside support against a Republican who has raised about $155,000. Markets price the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with the fundamentals pointing to a lopsided margin.
model.watch: A major late outside spending surge for Shinkle or an unexpected scandal involving Lasher could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Manhattan district open, but the seat's D+33 partisan lean makes it a very difficult target for Republicans. Micah Lasher has built a dominant financial position, raising over $3.3 million and benefiting from more than $10 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised only about $155,000 with no outside backing.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. Minor-party candidates trail far behind in fundraising. The forecast expects a wide Democratic margin with low but nonzero uncertainty, given the open seat and absence of polling.
